Treasury tool · English and Arabic

Numbers to Words Converter

Writes a financial amount out in words in English and Arabic for 156 currencies — the wording used on cheques, bills of exchange and bank letters — with correct Arabic grammatical agreement and no rounding.

Open demo

The tool on this site is the original converter restyled for the portfolio; its conversion code is unchanged.

The problem

Amounts in words must match the figures exactly. In Arabic the wording also changes with the number: the gender of the currency, the dual form for two, and the case of the counted noun all depend on the amount, which makes manual wording slow and error-prone.

What it does

  • English and Arabic wording side by side, with the “… and 50/100 … Only” and “… فقط لا غير” conventions.
  • Arabic rules for gender agreement, the dual, the counted noun after 3–10 and 11–99, and construct forms such as “ألفا ريال”.
  • 156 currencies, including three-decimal currencies such as the Kuwaiti dinar, plus a custom currency definition.
  • Validation that rejects malformed amounts or extra decimals with a clear message instead of rounding them.
  • Accepts Arabic-Indic digits, inserts thousands separators while typing, and copies either wording with one click.
  • A built-in check suite of 154 cases covering formatting, grammar and error handling.
